A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same FIM-SDE paper and complete Appendices A-H. Text comparison and rendering of all 34 pages support reliable comparison of the text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original SDE simulation experiments, evaluations on four real-world datasets, and ablation results in Section 5 and Appendices G-H.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original empirical evaluations and ablations, including the results in Tables 1-3 and 6-12.

M1.justification: The synthetic-prior construction, FIM-SDE architecture, training objectives, normalization, inference, and dense/sparse finetuning procedures are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices C-D.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic training coverage, eight canonical SDE systems, and four real-world datasets: wind, oil, Facebook, and Tesla. Noise, sampling, and initial-condition scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical: SparseGP and BISDE in Table 1, LatentSDE in Table 2, and BISDE and LatentSDE in Table 3. Appendix comparisons also retain the same methods.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes and splits, preprocessing, noise and sampling settings, MMD/MSE metrics, and training/finetuning budgets match throughout Section 5 and Appendices C-H.

E4.justification: Appendix H retains the same ablations of model/data size, polynomial degree, and context size. Noise/sparsity robustness tests, convergence analyses, and qualitative examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: The five repetitions of canonical experiments, five-fold real-world evaluations, and associated mean/standard-deviation reporting are unchanged. Appendix statistical reporting also matches.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and qualitative findings are identical, including main Tables 1-3, appendix Tables 6-12, and Figures 2-6. No results are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: The SDE definitions, mathematical assumptions, objectives, and derivations in Sections 3-4 and Appendices B-D are unchanged. No mathematical reasoning or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about in-context drift/diffusion estimation, generalization, and rapid finetuning.

C2.justification: Interpretations of finetuning and Lorenz diffusion bias are unchanged. The limitations concerning polynomial priors, low dimensionality, and data-generation rejection rates remain identical.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training duration, baseline configurations, and data-processing instructions are unchanged. Both versions provide the same stated model, code, and tutorial access information.

R1.justification: The complete reference lists match after accounting for page breaks. Section 2 and Appendix A retain identical related-work discussion and research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds a sentence acknowledging César Ojeda's DFG support under Project-ID 318763901, SFB1294, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded acknowledgment causes limited bibliography reflow across pages 11-14. Figures 1-6 and Tables 1-12 retain identical content, captions, structure, and placement; all appendix pages render identically.

improvement.justification: v3 adds a small funding-disclosure refinement on page 11, accompanied by an updated arXiv stamp and bibliography reflow. With scientific content, appendices, explanations, and reproducibility information unchanged, these edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
